Hi Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the three asks you mentioned so we can follow up with engineering: 

1) Exact scope of request/response logs you need for debugging vs. what must be retained for auditing.
2) Whether trace IDs in headers can be pseudonymized or require full residency/retention (and any format restrictions).
3) Confirmation on residency: logs must be stored in us-east-1 for 7 years per your compliance note, or is shorter retention acceptable for dev traces?

Action items we promised:
- Attach a short sample of request/response log format we capture today (redwood-owned format) — see attached sample-request-response-logs.txt.
- Draft redaction patterns we can apply to headers (trace ids, cookies, auth headers) and share a proposal — attaching initial PDF.
- Share a recording of the session for your records (demo-recording-20240729.mp4 attached).

Next steps: if you can confirm the three bullets above by EOD Tuesday (30 Jul) we’ll have a scoped plan and an engineering ETA for a POC. If you want us to prepare a masked-sample set (ours or yours) for validation, say the word and we’ll generate one.

Hi Kimberly —

Great demo — appreciate the walkthrough. Quick answers: 

1) Debug vs audit: Debug traces can be ephemeral (30 days) but audit logs must be retained 7 years. Audit logs are the system-level request/response pairs for billing and incident review.
2) Trace IDs: We cannot store raw customer trace IDs long-term. We need them pseudonymized (SHA-256 salted hash is acceptable) for the archived audit logs so they remain linkable within MediTrace but not reversible. For short-lived debugging caches (within 30 days) you can keep original trace IDs in memory as long as they are not exported to longer-term storage unredacted.
3) Residency: Audit retention must be in us-east-1 and meet your SOC2 export controls. Debug caches can be region-flexible.

A couple of asks from our side: 
- Can you share an example of the pseudonymization approach applied to the header values (we’d like to review pattern matching for trace id detection).
- For headers like X-Forwarded-For and Cookie, we will expect either removal or tokenization; please include both options in the proposal.

Thanks — I’ll loop security in if needed for a deeper tech review.

—Carlos

Hi Carlos —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. I pulled together a short technical note below and included two options for handling sensitive headers + trace ids. I attached the redaction-proposal.pdf with examples and pseudocode.

Option A — Pseudonymize then store in audit archive
- Identify header patterns: trace ids (regex: [A-Fa-f0-9]{24,64}), X-Request-ID, X-Trace-ID, any header named TRACEID/TRACE-ID.
- Apply HMAC-SHA256 with a MediTrace-managed salt (salt rotates quarterly) to generate non-reversible tokens.
- Store token in audit archive alongside metadata (timestamp, model-id, route) — archive located in us-east-1 and retained 7 years.

Option B — Strip from archived logs, keep ephemeral reference
- Remove trace id header from any log written to long-term archive.
- Persist mapping (tokenized) only to short-lived debug cache with TTL=30d.
- Map can be exported to MediTrace upon formal request and audit.

Other header controls we recommend:
- Remove Authorization, set Authorization-presence flag (boolean) so auditors know auth was present but not the token.
- Hash IPs (truncate to /24 + HMAC) or remove entirely depending on legal requirements.

Next steps from engineering side:
- We can prepare a masked sample set derived from your sample logs and run a verification there — estimated 3 business days to produce and 2 days for joint review.
- If MediTrace requires on-prem retention with customer KMS, that’s doable under Redwood Private; we’ll scope separately.

Kimberly — can you confirm MediTrace wants Option A or B for audit storage? Once they confirm, Jonas and I will provide an ETA for the POC and a short runbook for validation.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Monica — thanks for the clear options. MediTrace prefers Option A (HMAC/SHA256 pseudonymization with customer-managed salt). A few clarifications: 

- Salt management: we want to manage the salt in our KMS and provide Redwood with a wrapped key or HSM integration details. Is there an integration guide?
- Retention: confirm that tokens + metadata will be immutable for the 7-year archive and accessible only to MediTrace via audit exports.
- Sample verification: yes please prepare the masked sample set. We’d like the sample to include both a trace id that matches the regex and a header with multiple trace-like fields.

If you can send a short integration note about the salt/HSM flow and a proposed timeline for the POC by EOD Wednesday (31 Jul), I’ll route to our infra security for sign-off.

Thanks — Carlos
